content:
Quick answer: The best siding marketing agency already works with siding or exterior contractors and can handle SEO, Google Ads and a website built to book estimates. Look for material-specific pages, local search, reviews with project photos, and reporting on booked estimates and signed jobs, not just clicks.

Key Takeaways

Siding is a high-ticket, seasonal purchase, and homeowners often compare several contractors before they sign. Good siding marketing starts with a page for each material, such as vinyl, fiber cement and engineered wood, and for each city you serve. Your Google Business Profile, reviews and before-and-after photos win local trust. Google Ads and Local Services Ads bring estimates while SEO builds. If you hold a manufacturer certification, show it. Some agencies serve only one siding company per area, while lead sellers share leads with your competitors. Before you hire, ask which siding clients the agency serves, who owns your accounts and how it tracks booked estimates.

What a Siding Marketing Agency Does

A siding marketing agency gets your company in front of homeowners when they're shopping for new siding, and turns that interest into booked estimates. Siding is a high-ticket, seasonal job, and homeowners research materials before they call anyone. The main channels are SEO, Google Ads, your website and reviews. This post covers what good siding marketing includes, then compares agencies. It is written for owners shopping for home improvement marketing help.

What Good Siding Marketing Includes

Pages for Each Siding Material and City

Homeowners search by material and town, so give each one its own page. Strong siding SEO starts with pages for the materials you install, such as vinyl, fiber cement, engineered wood, metal and stucco repair. Add pages for siding repair and siding replacement, plus city pages that show real local projects. Name a manufacturer only if you are certified or install that brand. Here is how the pages can look:
SearchPage URLPage title
fiber cement siding Denver/fiber-cement-siding-denverFiber Cement Siding in Denver, CO
vinyl siding replacement Aurora/vinyl-siding-auroraVinyl Siding Replacement in Aurora, CO
siding repair Lakewood/siding-repair-lakewoodSiding Repair in Lakewood, CO

Websites Built to Book Estimates

A siding website has one job: turn a homeowner's research into a booked estimate. A good siding company web design loads fast on a phone and puts tap-to-call and an estimate form above the fold. Show before-and-after galleries sorted by material. Add warranty and certification badges only if you hold them, and a financing note only if you offer it. Link your service and city pages from the menu so visitors and Google can find them.

Local SEO, Reviews and Project Photos

Your Google Business Profile and reviews are what homeowners check before they call. Choose the siding contractor category, list every service and upload real project photos. Ask for a Google review after each job and reply to every one. Keep your name, address and phone number the same everywhere online. Steady review management builds the trust that closes high-ticket jobs.

Google Ads, Local Services Ads and Targeted Advertising

Google Ads bring estimate requests fast while your SEO builds. Build campaigns around material and city keywords, and add negative keywords such as DIY, siding panels for sale and jobs so you don't pay for the wrong clicks. Track every call so you know which ads book estimates. Local Services Ads can add a Google screened badge in areas and trades where Google offers them, so check availability for your market. Google Ads work well alongside geofencing and programmatic ads aimed at neighborhoods near your current jobs.

Storm Damage, Seasons and Trust Signals

Siding demand rises after storms and in good building weather, so plan pages and budgets ahead. Build storm and hail damage pages before storm season, and raise ad budgets in your peak months. See our guide to storm season SEO for the same approach. Never promise to pay or waive an insurance deductible, because some states, including Texas, prohibit it. Check your own state's rules. Show EPA lead-safe (RRP) certification if you hold it, since work on homes built before 1978 can disturb lead paint. Show manufacturer certifications only if you hold them.

SEO vs PPC vs Lead Sellers for Siding Contractors

Siding contractors get leads from three main sources, and each has a different cost and level of control.
SourceSpeedCost modelWho owns the lead
SEOMonthsMonthly feeYou own it
Google Ads and Local Services AdsDaysPay per click or leadYou own it
Lead sellers like ModernizeFastPay per leadOften shared with other contractors
Modernize is a lead seller, not an agency. Its leads are often shared among several contractors. Many contractors use lead sellers to fill gaps while their own SEO grows.

How We Picked These Siding Marketing Agencies

We compared each agency on six points that matter to siding and exterior contractors:
  • Siding or exterior clients today
  • SEO and material pages
  • Google Ads and Local Services Ads
  • Websites built for estimates
  • Tracking of booked estimates and signed jobs
  • Contract terms, account ownership and market exclusivity

6. Blue Corona: Data-Driven Siding Marketing

About: Blue Corona is a data-focused agency that tracks leads back to their source. That shows siding contractors which ad or page produced a call. Best for: Companies that want to see which channel pays.

Questions to Ask Before You Hire a Siding Marketing Agency

  1. Which siding or exterior contractors do you work with now? Experience with siding shortens the learning curve.
  2. Do you work with only one siding company per area? Shared markets mean your agency serves your competitor too.
  3. Who owns my website, ad accounts and Google profile? You should keep them if you leave.
  4. Do you track booked estimates and signed jobs? Clicks alone don't show what makes money.
  5. How long is the contract? Long lock-ins make it hard to switch if results lag.
  6. What are the fee and ad spend? Get both in writing, stated separately.

h1: Siding Company Marketing: The Best SEO, PPC and Web Design Agencies

faqs.question: What does a siding marketing agency do?
faqs.answer: It brings homeowners to your company through SEO, Google Ads, your website, reviews and local search. A good agency also tracks booked estimates and signed jobs so you can see what each channel brings in.

faqs.question: How do roofing and siding contractors advertise?
faqs.answer: Most use Google Ads and Local Services Ads for fast leads, SEO and a strong Google Business Profile for long-term leads, and yard signs and neighborhood ads near current jobs. Many also add storm damage campaigns after severe weather.

faqs.question: Is SEO or PPC better for siding companies?
faqs.answer: PPC brings estimate requests within days but stops when you stop paying. SEO takes months to build but keeps bringing leads at a lower cost over time. Most siding contractors use both.

faqs.question: How long does siding SEO take?
faqs.answer: Google Business Profile and review work can show movement within one to two months. New material and city pages usually take three to six months to rank, depending on local competition.

faqs.question: What should a siding company website include?
faqs.answer: Fast mobile pages, a page for each material and city, before-and-after photos, tap-to-call and estimate forms, and certifications or warranties you actually hold.

faqs.question: Which companies help contractors market manufactured home siding?
faqs.answer: Home improvement marketing agencies can build pages and ads aimed at manufactured and mobile home owners. Ask any agency whether it has done this before and how it targets those homeowners in your area.

faqs.question: Should I buy siding leads?
faqs.answer: Bought leads arrive fast but are often shared with other contractors. Leads from your own website, ads and Google profile are yours alone. Many contractors use both while their own lead flow grows.
